subject: humanities
passage: Plays at the Globe, the open-air London theater where many of Shakespeare's works were first performed, took place in the afternoon by natural daylight. Since there was no way to darken the stage, audiences had to be told when a scene happened at night. <u>Characters therefore often mention the darkness directly, as when a nobleman in Macbeth observes that the heavens have put out their candles.</u> Actors might also carry torches or lanterns, objects that were useless in the bright afternoon but signaled that spectators should imagine night.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It suggests that Globe audiences were often confused about when scenes took place.
choices.B: It gives an example of one way plays dealt with the limitation described in the previous sentence.
choices.C: It explains why the Globe was built as an open-air theater.
choices.D: It argues that Macbeth was written to be performed after dark.

explanation.why: The previous sentence states a problem: the stage could not be darkened, so audiences "had to be told" when a scene was at night. The underlined sentence, beginning with "therefore," describes one solution, characters mentioning the darkness, and gives an example from Macbeth. The final sentence adds a second method, torches and lanterns.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The sentence shows how plays prevented confusion; it does not say audiences were often confused.
explanation.B: Correct. Having characters talk about the darkness is one way plays told daylight audiences that a scene took place at night.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text never explains why the Globe had no roof.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says plays at the Globe were performed in daylight; the Macbeth line is an example of describing night, not evidence that the play was staged at night.
